headline: Recommended holding the Plan E City Charter review request and a related City Clerk communication; placed another communication on file.
summary: Sixteen residents spoke on charter review, fifteen in favor and one in opposition. Members discussed charter change options and asked the City Clerk and City Solicitor for reports. Members voted 3-0 to recommend holding the charter review order and a related communication.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the May 20, 2026 meeting, 3-0.
Recommended holding the Plan E City Charter review order (item 3a) and the City Clerk's communication on charter review options (item 4a), 3-0.
Recommended placing the City Clerk's communication on advertisements for the August 17, 2026 meeting on file, 3-0.
Recommended placing the City Manager's communication on a process to establish a charter review commission on file, 3-0.

Transmitting an informational communication relative to various options available for 
making changes to the City Charter.
# 14b CC July 21, 2026
a.
August 17, 2026 Page 4 of 8Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee
Chairperson Councilor Mitra read the item and moved to take the item up collectively with Item 
#3a. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized the City Solicitor, who provided an overview of the 
processes in place to amend the City Charter, which included what a municipal charter is, a 
history of Worcester’s charters, the process used to adopt a home rule charter, the process to 
establish and the role of a Charter Review Commission, the process used to adopt a charter 
amendment by special legislation, methods related to charter amendments, and modern charter 
provisions.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized the City Clerk, who provided an overview of the process 
to establish a Charter Review Commission, which also included the process relative to file and run 
as a Charter Review Commission candidate and the process relative to charter amendments by 
special act. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra then recognized the following Speakers:
1. Fred Nathan, Worcester resident, spoke in opposition to a charter review
2. Gary Hunter, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
3. Sue Mailman, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
4. Randy Feldman, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
5. Tom Marino, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
6. Steve Hart, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
7. Keith Linhares, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
8. Dante Comparetto, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
9. Francesco Bivona, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
10. Joshua Croke, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
11. Greg Waters, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
12. Jack Murray, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
13. Feanna Jattan-Singh, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
14. Dominick Calsolaro, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
15. Sarah Moore, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
16. Martha Assefa, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of a charter review
Chairperson Councilor Mitra discussed the required 15% certified voter signatures to establish a 
Charter Review Commission, charter amendment options that do not require voter signatures 
such as through special acts, proposed ordinance amendments to amend various roles and 
responsibilities of boards and commissions, and the roles of standing committees relative to 
ordinance amendments with the City Solicitor, City Clerk, and Speaker #4. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra brought forth the following Chairman’s Order: “Request City 
Clerk work with City Solicitor to provide City Council with a report detailing City Council’s role 
related to ordinance changes.” 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra then brought forth the following Chairman’s Order: “Request City 
Clerk work with City Solicitor to provide City Council with a report detailing possible charter 
changes that could be done without the creation of a Charter Review Commission in addition to 
charter changes that require approval of such a commission.”
Chairperson Councilor Mitra discussed the feasibility of providing a report detailing resident 
testimony brought forth during Public Participation with the City Clerk. 
August 17, 2026 Page 5 of 8Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee
Chairperson Councilor Mitra brought forth the following Chairman’s Order: “Request City 
Clerk provide City Council with a report detailing resident testimony brought forth at the 
Monday, August 17, 2026 Standing Committee on Municipal and Legislative Operations meeting.”
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Rosen, who discussed the feasibility of 
acquiring 20,000 signatures, highlighted the importance of distinguishing the difference between 
charter review and charter change, a history of past charter reviews, increased public 
participation due to additional meeting advertisement methods, and the importance of reviewing 
the charter every ten (10) years.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Bergman, who discussed challenges in the city 
that would not be addressed by changing the form of government, a history of past Municipal and 
Legislative Operations Committee meetings discussing charter review, the feasibility of placing a 
non-binding referendum on the next local election ballot to gauge the opinion of the city’s voters 
relative to charter review, highlighted the importance of amending parts of the city’s charter as 
needed prior to finalizing a full charter review, spoke in opposition to the notion of reducing the 
City Manager’s salary for the purpose of making the positions of Mayor and City Councilor 
full-time positions, and the importance of resident civic engagement and the duty to vote in 
elections. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra discussed best methods to process a charter review in lieu of 
collecting 15% of voter signatures to establish a Charter Review Commission. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra then discussed the intended purpose of the meeting as to provide 
education related to the review process and methods for making changes to the city’s charter with 
Speaker #2.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Rosen, who discussed the importance of the 
City Council going on record to support a charter review. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Bergman, who highlighted the need for a 
non-binding referendum for the next local election. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Rosen, who moved for the following 
Chairman’s Resolution: “That the Standing Committee on Municipal and Legislative Operations 
does hereby recommend and support the efforts to review the current modified Plan E City 
Charter.” – Not Put. 
Councilor Rosen then discussed the process relative for residents to start collecting signatures for a 
Charter Review Commission and a history of the signatures obtained in the 1980’s when the 
process was first initiated with the City Clerk. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Bergman, who discussed the need for 
additional resident engagement to understand the needs of the majority residents in the city. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Rosen, who discussed feasible next steps to 
review the city’s charter, that the city’s charter has not had a comprehensive review in forty (40) 
years, reviewing resident testimony and providing City Council with a report detailing feasible 
charter amendment options based on said testimony with the City Clerk. 
August 17, 2026 Page 6 of 8Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Bergman, who moved to amend Councilor 
Rosen’s motion to read as: “That the Standing Committee on Municipal and Legislative 
Operations does here by recommend that the full City Council support all efforts of all residents 
in reviewing any charter change.” – Not Put.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Rosen, who moved to hold the motion until 
the Communications of the City Clerk relative to charter review processes and resident testimony 
are brought forth to the City Council with the City Clerk. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra brought forth the following Chairman’s Order: “Request City 
Clerk provide City Council with a report detailing the process required to place a non -binding 
question on the ballot of the upcoming local election.”
Chairperson Councilor Mitra moved for a roll call vote to recommend the items be held. 
Recommend Hold on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
